title: Walking Dead: Here's Negan - Board Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ASSnCNI-KlM

Daniel (@dungeondive) is not a Walking Dead fan — he knows who Negan is and little more — so Mantic's Here's Negan was nowhere on his radar until reviews from Black Jack Legacy and Guerrilla Miniature Games sold it to him as a more soloable Space Hulk. Several plays in, he likes it a lot, and apologises to Mantic: after Dungeon Saga he had written them off; Hellboy and this changed his mind.

You play Negan's lieutenants securing the Sanctuary factory room by room. Rooms are dealt from a deck (flooded, rotten floors, vents, barricades), and unseen walkers are Space Hulk-style blips that reveal only on entering line of sight; flooded rooms hide even the blips. Noise draws walkers in and raises the threat; secured rooms lower it.

The standout is Negan himself. Nobody controls him. He walks a scripted path driven by his own card deck: sulking, raging, poking survivors with Lucille, and handing out reputation to whoever is standing nearest rather than whoever earned it. In Daniel's game Sherry and Tara did the heavy lifting while a straggler named John collected the praise — pure zombie fiction. It's co-op with a competitive edge, since you are all vying for Negan's approval across the campaign.

The catches: $60 is steep for a small box, and there is only one enemy type. He'd love a small expansion adding a rival human squad, because in zombie fiction the real enemies are always other humans.

----

Negan is run by a deck of cards and rewards whoever happens to be closest. What's the best example you've played of an uncontrolled NPC generating the story?
